title: Reply: the same innate notes that show divinity also show essential integrity
source_text: XXXVIII. Hic certe Pontificii constringuntur propriis laqueis, neque se possunt expedire quin objectioni suae responsionem subministrent. Sed respondeo quod sicut non opus est alio Dei verbo, cujus testimonio probetur Scripturam sacram esse divinam, quia Scriptura sacra est prima fidei regula, in qua fides nostra sistitur: Ipsa vero per se innotescere potest ex signis & notis insitis, aliisque argumentis & credendi motivis, quibus possunt fideles sufficienter moveri ut illam amplectantur ceu veram & divinam: ita quoque non opus est alio Dei verbo unde discamus Scripturam incorruptam & integram esse. Nam unde discimus illam esse divinam, inde discimus illam integram & sinceram esse, in rebus saltem momentosis & essentialibus.
pass_a_gloss: Here certainly the Pontificians are constrained by their own snares, nor can they extricate themselves without supplying a response to their own objection. But I answer that just as there is no need of another word of God by whose testimony it is proved that sacred Scripture is divine, because sacred Scripture is the first rule of faith in which our faith is stopped: But it itself can become known through itself from implanted signs and notes, and other arguments and motives of believing, by which the faithful can be sufficiently moved to embrace it as true and divine: so also there is no need of another word of God whence we may learn that Scripture is uncorrupted and integral. For whence we learn that it is divine, thence we learn that it is integral and sincere, at least in things momentous and essential.
pass_b_english: Rome is caught in its own snare — the integrity demand forces the reply their Scripture objection needs.
As Scripture needs no second word to prove its divinity, because it is the first rule known by innate signs and motives,
so it needs no second word to prove it uncorrupted and integral.
The same path that shows it divine shows it integral and sincere — at least in momentous and essential matters.
